column3: The Hebrew explicitly names David as the speaker and uses plural lands of Israel; BSB uses he and singular land.
The Hebrew says the assembly said to do so because the matter was right in everyone’s eyes; BSB moves the reason first and summarizes their speech as agreement.
The Hebrew says Shihor of Egypt without explicitly calling it a river; BSB supplies River.
The Hebrew says Uzzah stretched out his hand to grasp the ark; BSB describes reaching out and actually taking hold of it.
The Hebrew repeats the bursting word as verb and noun; BSB describes bursting forth without that repetition.
The Hebrew repeats David’s name and says bringing the ark to himself; BSB uses he and moving it with him.
The Hebrew repeats Obed-edom’s name and twice uses house for his household; BSB uses family and later his household.
